column1:
- Policy action: The FOMC delivered a 50 bp cut (to 4.75–5.00%), lowered IORB (4.9%) and ON RRP (4.8%), and expressed greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2%. QT continues. Net effect: easier front-end financial conditions.
- Beige Book cross-check (Aug 26, 2024, Cleveland Fed): Districts reported economic activity that was flat to modest, with consumer spending uneven. Labor markets continued to cool—job gains slowed and unemployment edged up—but remain relatively tight; wage growth moderated overall with lingering pockets of pressure for workers with specialized skills and skilled trades. Price increases slowed to modest. CRE conditions remained weak with valuation/refinancing concerns; manufacturing was mixed; residential real estate activity was constrained by tight inventories and financing costs. Many firms were cautious about the outlook.
- Credit channel: Beige Book anecdotes about tighter lending standards and soft demand align with SLOOS—ongoing tightening in C&I, broad CRE softness, and stricter consumer credit with gradually rising delinquencies—implying slower transmission of monetary easing to Main Street, especially for small businesses and CRE.
- Implication: The dovish policy impulse is supportive for financial conditions and risk assets, but Beige Book and SLOOS evidence of cooling activity, moderating wages/prices, and restrictive bank credit tempers the boost versus a purely dovish read.

Net: Moderately positive, but more constrained than an FOMC-statement-only view.
